body:
Hi, 

Thank you for reporting an issue. Could you provide a reproduction on stackblitz to help us investigate the issue ?

@phihochzwei thanks for reporting an issue. It'd be very helpful if you could try to narrow down the problem to see which pattern is causing this issue. Once you have a pattern that is causing the problem, we can perform further investigation and help to find a solution. To speed up the investigation, it'd be great to have a minimal repro (in a form of a GitHub repository) @JeanMeche mentioned above. Note: do **not** share the code of your application, try to create a new `ng new` application and use a pattern from your application that is causing the problem.

@phihochzwei as a temporary solution, if the problem is isolated to one of the components, you can try to opt that component out of hydration using the `ngSkipHydration` attribute as described in [hydration guide](https://angular.io/guide/hydration#how-to-skip-hydration-for-particular-components).

rename.from: TypeError: hostElement.hasAttribute is not a function
rename.to: TypeError when hydration is enabled (hostElement.hasAttribute is not a function)

body:
Hi @AndrewKushnir  

thanks for the answer. Actually, narrowing it down is my biggest problem here, since the project is quite big. What I found "so far" was, that within ALL OF THE CODE within the whole project ( I even scanned node_modules), the only place where hostElement.hasAttribute gets used seems to be within material. But I will try my best.

It seems, that the error is caused by the check for availability of the ngSkipHydration-flag itself:

`const hostElement=lView[HOST];hostElement&&!hostElement.hasAttribute(SKIP_HYDRATION_ATTR_NAME)` is where it is thrown.

I event tried adding ngSkipHydration to my app.component, but still no success

@phihochzwei right, the error is coming from this code:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/b3730081c3ddc7726c6fb1272e97ee6862d3b3a4/packages/core/src/hydration/annotate.ts#L111-L113

and the `hostElement` at that moment is expected to be a element node (which is a component host node). Based on the error message, it looks like it's either a comment node, a text node or some other object. We'd need to understand what this object is and under which circumstances this happens.

As a next step in the investigation, you can try updating the code in the `node_modules` or in the generated `main.js` that is used to run the app on the server and output some information into a console: like `hostElement.nodeType` and `hostElement.textContent` (if it's a DOM node) and may be try to stringify the value (for ex. using `JSON.stringify`) if it's not a DOM node.

Please let us know what you find.

@AndrewKushnir  Thank you all so much for your help and time. 

I added some console.logs and it seems, that hostElement at this point is not an element node but an array WITH element nodes (according to the console log 125). When I access the first element of this array, it returns me my app.component.

In addition: If I change the code to 

...hostElement. && !Array.isArray(hostElement) && hostElement.hasAttribut...  the page gets rendered. But my uneducated guess would be, that clientHydration is then completely skipped

@phihochzwei thanks for additional information. It'd be very helpful to understand why the `hostElement` is an array at that point. It looks like this is your root component, so I'm curious which bootstrapping method do you use for your application?
